solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Weatherproof coat a nosy person talked of?

indicators.note: talked of signals that we want a word as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: a nosy parker is a British idiom for someone who pries into others' business

explanation.surface: A riddle about which rainproof garment a busybody might be called in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nosy parker' is a British name for a busybody; said aloud, PARKER matches the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof jacket worn against rain and cold is exactly this kind of garment.

clue.text: Forked out to obtain large tartan cloth

indicators.note: the paying word takes in, or obtains, the size letter inside itself

parts.note: forked out is slang for paid money
L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone paid up to get a big piece of tartan fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked woollen fabric in a Scottish pattern is the textile this word names.

clue.text: Reportedly bucketing down on the throne?

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word's sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: bucketing down is British slang for pouring with rain

explanation.surface: A whimsical picture of a monarch sitting on the throne while it pours.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who is on the throne is currently ruling, the sense of this participle.

clue.text: A team apart!

parts.note: a side is a sports team, as in a football side

explanation.surface: An exclamation that one team stands apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart and set to one side are synonyms, both meaning separately.

clue.text: Back university's later presentation of bill

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it, a verb sense
Reading is an English town with a university, used here for the institution

explanation.surface: Supporting a university's subsequent bill presentation, a phrase from parliamentary procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in southern England with a well-known university.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament a bill passes through stages; this is the debate stage after its first introduction.

clue.text: Followers carrying English money in French street

indicators.note: carrying signals that the street word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: rue is French for street
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A band of supporters bearing English cash along a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is dated British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage of attendants accompanying an important person is a group of followers.

clue.text: Lightweight hat — best on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest lightweight hat to be found on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A topi is a pith helmet, the sun hat of colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith helmet worn in hot climates is a light sun hat known by this name.

clue.text: Study Pope's last lines outside a priest's office

indicators.note: outside signals that the run of letters sits around the single letter

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: A study of a pontiff's final lines, set outside a cleric's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope's last' is the letter E; 'lines' is the railway abbreviation, and 'outside' wraps the whole run around 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean holds a church office; the post or position he holds is called this.

clue.text: Dock worker rode out with street girl

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: out suggests the letters have been put out of order

explanation.surface: A docker rides away accompanied by a girl from the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the riding word into DORE; the street and girl come first in the answer despite following it in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A man employed to load and unload ships in port is a docker or longshoreman.

clue.text: Excuse a former politician invented originally

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a party that later merged into the Liberal Democrats

indicators.note: originally points to the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: An ex-politician's excuse was, in the first place, made up.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere at the time is a defence, loosely any pretext.

clue.text: Work in pub mostly, accepting Oscar's point of view

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: accepting signals that the shortened word takes a letter inside it
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: an inn is a pub
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's views offered while working in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the pub word, and 'accepting' slips Oscar inside what is left, giving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or belief someone holds is their standpoint or judgement.

clue.text: Debt-collector gone mad in underground cell

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

indicators.note: mad indicates the letters are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: A bailiff who has lost his mind sits in a basement prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark prison chamber beneath a castle is the classic place for captives.

clue.text: Percussionist beginning to drink spirit by sea in Boulogne?

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: rum is a spirit
mer is French for sea, Boulogne being a French port

explanation.surface: A musician starts drinking by the French seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the drums is a player of percussion.

clue.text: Flower girl's stated recipe for getting rich?

indicators.note: stated means spoken aloud, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: the advice is to marry gold, i.e. wed someone wealthy

explanation.surface: A flower girl announces her plan to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' is one phrase on the surface, but 'Flower' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a garden plant with orange or yellow blooms.

clue.text: City's way to divide fare in old-time feast

indicators.note: to divide signals that one piece splits the other by going inside it

parts.note: cheer once meant food and drink at a feast
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: How a city shares out the food at a historical banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to divide' puts ST into CHEER as CHE-ST-ER. Chester is a historic city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a walled cathedral city in Cheshire, England.

clue.text: Assume identity of quality paper without delay

parts.note: to be someone is to assume that person's identity
The Times is a British broadsheet newspaper

explanation.surface: Impersonating a serious newspaper, perhaps as a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adverb means early or promptly, so with no delay.

clue.text: Verbal greeting to girl revealing sanitary practices?

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Hi, Jean is a greeting to a girl

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a girl exposes something about cleanliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the set of habits of cleanliness that preserve health.

clue.text: Sale involving union leader in suit

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action

indicators.note: leader takes the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A sale involving a trade union boss, who is wearing a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Government emergency committee's firm supporter?

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Asks whether the crisis committee is a staunch backer.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA is the UK government's crisis committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A.
explanation.definitionFit: This acronym names the British cabinet committee convened for national crises.

clue.text: In London, a director's lowest point

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: A London director has hit rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom or worst moment of something is its low point, opposite the zenith.

clue.text: Main sentence describing guillemot, for example

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
bird is slang for a prison sentence (birdlime, time)

explanation.surface: A key sentence describing one kind of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is one of many birds that live along coasts and feed at sea.

clue.text: Part of church left abandoned by mistake

indicators.note: abandoned means dropped, so the letter goes from the longer word

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A section of a church was left deserted through an error.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is this architectural feature.

clue.text: Secondary thoroughfare of some width

definitions.meaning: in Britain a ... is a minor route below an A road

explanation.surface: A minor road that is reasonably wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as B plus road it is a lesser British road; as one word it means wide.

clue.text: Eg Asian editor initially more rigid about article

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
sterner means stricter, more rigid

explanation.surface: An Asian editor is at first stricter about an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Asia, the East, is an inhabitant of the eastern world.

clue.text: Person summing up poisonous snake

definitions.meaning: the viper, Britain's only venomous snake

explanation.surface: A person totting up figures, or a venomous reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: One who totals numbers, and also the common European viper.
